item.title: Calls for fair compensation for women displaced by lithium mining in Zimbabwe
item.description: The government has been urged to introduce a fair and transparent compensation system for communities displaced by lithium mining, with particular focus on protecting women’s land rights.

item.title: Government warns of fraudulent overseas job schemes
item.description: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Trade has warned Zimbabweans to exercise caution when accepting foreign job offers amid growing reports of citizens who are lured abroad under false promises of lucrative employment, noting that “most” of the recruitment agencies operate in digital spaces outside the country’s regulatory reach, making their activities difficult for authorities to monitor.

item.title: Residents cry foul over four-month power outage
item.description: Some residents in parts of Pumula, Bulawayo, have gone for more than four months without electricity following an incident that damaged electrical cables and a transformer servicing at least 121 households.

item.title: Chatunga Mugabe Abandons Bail Bid, Enters Plea Talks With State
item.description: Bellarmine Chatunga Mugabe, the son of the late Zimbabwean president Robert Mugabe, and his co-accused, Tobias Mugabe Matonhodze, have abandoned their bid for bail and opted to enter plea negotiations with the state.

item.title: Cabinet Adopts New Consumer Protection Policy
item.description: Cabinet on Tuesday, 10 March, considered and approved the Consumer Protection Policy, which, among other things, aims to regulate the supply of goods and services, safeguard the rights of consumers, and promote fair trading practices in the marketplace.

item.title: Proposed Constitutional Amendments Don’t Require Referendum, Says Former COPAC Co-Chair
item.description: Former ZANU PF Secretary for Legal Affairs, Paul Mangwana, has said that President Emmerson Mnangagwa will not gain an extra term under the current constitutional changes, as he is set to serve only two more years—less than a full term, which the law defines as between three and five years.

item.title: Chibaya, Four Other Opposition Activists Acquitted In High Court After Appeal
item.description: The High Court in Harare has overturned the conviction of three former opposition legislators and two Harare residents who had been found guilty of promoting public violence after their arrest three years ago for allegedly taking part in an unsanctioned gathering.

item.title: Those who drafted the 2013 term limits to get rid of Mugabe in order to take over power are now victims of their own trap
item.description: The irony of political history is frequently found in the permanence of the traps we set for others.

item.title: The removal of direct presidential elections is an unforgivable betrayal of the liberation struggle
item.description: When personal greed overrides collective national sacrifice.

item.title: Jonathan Moyo, Ziyambi Ziyambi, Jacob Mudenda and Emmerson Mnangagwa want Zimbabweans to accept human stool for cake
item.description: Do not play with people’s minds – God is Watching – Learned Judges and Defence Lawyers, Don’t fall Victim to this stupid trick
